These spectacular places encompass a broad range of breathtaking natural features, including coral reefs, kelp forests, beaches, tidewater glaciers, estuaries, sand dunes, islands, and more. Many are also gateways for exploring the nation's rich maritime and military history, including lighthouses, forts, and battlefields. The most well-known opinions are those released or announced in cases in which the Court has heard oral argument. Each opinion sets out the Court’s judgment and its reasoning and may include the majority or principal opinion as well as any concurring or dissenting opinions. All opinions in a single case are published together and are prefaced by a syllabus prepared by the Reporter of Decisions that summarizes the Court’s decision. The Justice who authors the majority or principal opinion often will summarize the opinion from the bench during a Court session. The Court may also dispose of cases in per curiam opinions, which do not identify the author. These cases frequently resolve cases summarily, often without oral argument. But per curiam opinions have sometimes been issued in argued cases. In-chambers opinions are written by an individual Justice to dispose of an application by a party for interim relief, e.g. , for a stay of the judgment of the court below, for vacation of a stay, or for a temporary injunction. Try again ADVANCED SEARCH DOCKET SEARCH Search Home > Oral Arguments Argument Transcripts Argument Audio Calendars and Lists Courtroom Seating Oral Arguments The Court holds oral argument in about 70-80 cases each year. The arguments are an opportunity for the Justices to ask questions directly of the attorneys representing the parties to the case, and for the attorneys to highlight arguments that they view as particularly important. Arguments are generally scheduled on specified Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings beginning on the first Monday in October, and continuing through the end of April. Typically, the Court holds two arguments each day beginning at 10:00 a.m. The days on which arguments are held are identified on the Court’s yearly calendar . The specific cases to be argued each day, and the attorneys scheduled to argue them, are identified on hearing lists for each session and on the day call for each argument session. The Court is currently conducting a pilot program in which members of the public may apply for Courtroom seating through an online lottery . During this pilot program, Courtroom seating will also be available to the public on a first-come, first-seated basis. An audio feed of the argument is live-streamed on the Court's website, and the Court posts the audio later in the day. Size comparisons for PM particles PM stands for particulate matter (also called particle pollution): the term for a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets found in the air. Some particles, such as dust, dirt, soot, or smoke, are large or dark enough to be seen with the naked eye. Others are so small they can only be detected using an electron microscope. Particle pollution includes: PM 10 : inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 10 micrometers and smaller; and PM 2.5 : fine inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 2.5 micrometers and smaller. How small is 2.5 micrometers? Think about a single hair from your head. The average human hair is about 70 micrometers in diameter – making it 30 times larger than the largest fine particle. Sources of PM These particles come in many sizes and shapes and can be made up of hundreds of different chemicals. McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed. But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers. Petroglyphs , images carved into rock, and pictographs , images painted onto rock surfaces, take both abstract forms, such as spirals and lines, and recognizable animal or human shapes. pages.text: Posters - Frequently Asked Questions | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Posters - Frequently Asked Questions Question : Can I use the "six-in-one" or other large combination poster rather than separate posters? Can I get a "six-in-one" poster from the U.S. Department of Labor? Answer : If all the posters you are required to post are in the “six-in-one” poster and each individual poster meets the size requirements of the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) then you may use it. There are only two posters where the regulations specify a size (the OSHA poster and Executive Order 13496 poster), but all federal workplace posters must be easily readable. Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA) Poster – The regulations state that reproductions or facsimiles of the poster shall be at least 8 1/2 by 14 inches with 10-point type. The Executive Order 13496: Notification of Employee Rights Under Federal Labor Laws Poster – Contractors may reproduce the poster but may only use exact duplicates. The poster must be 11 by 17 inches. The U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) provides posters in the proper size for free on the DOL Poster Topic page or by calling the Department at 1-866-4-USA-DOL (1-866-487-2365). However, DOL does not supply such “six-in-one” posters since different employers have different notice requirements. Protect yourself from dengue by avoiding mosquito bites. There are no dengue vaccines currently available in the United States. Opioids, mainly illegally made fentanyl, are involved in the highest percentage of overdose deaths. Ways to prevent opioid overdose are to improve opioid prescribing, reduce exposure to opioids, prevent illegal opioid use and prescription opioid misuse, and treat opioid use disorder. Preventing Type 2 Diabetes May 15, 2024 Español Key points Prediabetes is a serious health condition, and more than 2 in 5 U.S. adults have it. With early action, you can reverse prediabetes to prevent or delay type 2 diabetes. Find out if you have a high risk for prediabetes by taking the 1-minute risk test. What is prediabetes? Before developing type 2 diabetes, most people have prediabetes. This is when their blood sugar is higher than normal but not high enough yet for a type 2 diabetes diagnosis. In the United States, about 115 million adults have prediabetes; that's more than 2 in 5. There are usually no signs when you have prediabetes, which is why 8 in 10 people don't know they have it. You can have prediabetes for years and not know. Ready to find out where you stand? Take the 1-minute prediabetes risk test . If your score shows you have a high risk of prediabetes, visit your doctor for a simple blood test to confirm your result. pages.text: PSNI taking 'more robust' approach to e-bikes and scooters Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live PSNI taking 'more robust' approach to e-bikes and scooters 6 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Barry O'Connor , Claire Quinn and Niall Glynn , BBC News NI Third Street Studios Police helicopter footage shows a child on an e-scooter in Belfast city centre E-Scooters and e-bikes have "become a challenging issue" for the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI), the lead road safety officer has said. From 1 January until 31 October 2026 provisional figures show 473 of the machines were seized by the PSNI, 379 of which were e-scooters. In the two years between 1 September 2024 and 31 August 2026, provisional police figures also show there were 150 collisions involving e-scooters reported to the PSNI. There were two fatalities in that time and 45 people sustained serious injuries. "We have taken a more robust approach in dealing with the issue," Ch Supt Sam Donaldson said. Police Service of Northern Ireland Chief Superintendent Sam Donaldson said police are taking a robust approach "It's crucial there is a consistent approach by officers across Northern Ireland when dealing with the issue," he added. During a three-day operation in September, a six-year-old child was among those stopped by police and 65 e-bikes and e-scooters were seized. pages.text: Questions over Warwickshire Chief Constable appointment process Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Questions over police chief recruitment after candidate dropped 5 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Joan Cummins and Alec Blackman , West Midlands BBC/ Richard Forbes Emma Bond is currently the assistant chief constable of Police Scotland The Warwickshire Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) is facing questions over the recruitment of a new chief constable after withdrawing the preferred candidate's job offer. Emma Bond, currently Assistant Chief Constable at Police Scotland, was named in May as the preferred choice to replace Alex Franklin-Smith following his retirement in April. But more than four months later, the PCC announced that Bond's preferred candidate status had been withdrawn, meaning she will no longer take up the role. In a statement, Warwickshire PCC Philip Seccombe said no further comment would be made. However, the decision to effectively withdraw the job offer, which was subject to vetting, raises questions about the leadership of the county force. It comes after David Gardner, the current Acting Chief Constable, has already been appointed as the new head of Staffordshire Police, following a four week recruitment process. The PCC said arrangements would be announced to "to ensure continuity of leadership for Warwickshire Police", but gave no timetable. If you smoke, quitting is one of the best things you can do for your health. A real story Tiffany R. learned early in life that cigarettes cause premature death and disease : her mother died of smoking-related lung cancer when Tiffany was just 16. Tiffany, a participant in CDC's Tips From Former Smokers ® ( Tips ) ad campaign, said that she felt alone and afraid during her mother's illness. "And I felt it could have been prevented," she said. Even so, Tiffany herself wasn't able to quit smoking for good until her own daughter turned 16. "I didn't want my daughter to think, 'Wow, my mother loves cigarette smoking more than she cares about me,'" she said. pages.text: Rare Chinese vases found in Oxfordshire could fetch £50,000 Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Rare Chinese Qing dynasty vases could fetch £50,000 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ethan Gudge South of England Mallams The vases are expected to fetch up to £50,000 at an auction next week A pair of rare Chinese vases thought to date back from the 17th Century are estimated to fetch up to £50,000 when they go under the hammer next week. The two Chinese Famille Verte 'Ladies' Vases are thought to date back to the Kangxi period of the Qing dynasty, between 1662 and 1722. Auction house Mallam's explained that the vases had been in an Oxfordshire country house and represented "an extraordinary rediscovery of Chinese porcelain". The auctioneers, based in Cheltenham, estimate the "magnificent and important" pair of vases could sell for between £30,000 and £50,000 when they go up for sale on Wednesday. Robin Fisher, Mallams' Asian art expert said the sale offered "a rare opportunity to acquire a piece of documented collecting history" for potential buyers. Getty Images The pair of vases date back to the reign of the Kangxi Emperor Explaining the porcelains provenance, the auction house said they had been painted "in exceptionally vibrant famille verte enamels". Regulations EPA is called a regulatory agency because Congress authorizes us to write regulations that explain the technical, operational, and legal details necessary to implement laws. Regulations are mandatory requirements that can apply to individuals, businesses, state or local governments, non-profit institutions, or others.
